_fixture.description: Identical to 01-fixture-stripe-happy. Used to verify that re-delivering the same Stripe webhook (which Stripe does on slow webhook responses) does NOT create a duplicate Xero journal. The Idempotency Check finds the POSTED row and returns the original JournalID with idempotent: true.
_fixture.expected_outcome: HTTP 200, result=POSTED, idempotent=true, xero_journal_id matches the one returned by the first delivery of 01-fixture. No new posting_events row (the workflow exits at the Idempotency Decision Switch before any new DB writes). No new Xero ManualJournal call.
_fixture.replay_instructions: After running 01-fixture-stripe-happy to completion (payouts row is POSTED), replay this same webhook payload to POST {webhook_url}/stripe-payout-paid with a valid Stripe-Signature.

expected_idempotency_state.idempotency_check_returns: 1 row with status='POSTED' and the xero_journal_id from the first delivery
expected_idempotency_state.side_effects: NONE: no new payouts row, no new posting_events row, no Xero API call.
